Q1: Magnesium hydroxide exhibits a mixed hazard profile with several significant data gaps. It shows demonstrated low to moderate hazards for inhalation and oral exposure (Tier 3). However, a more detailed assessment (Tier 2) indicates potential dermal and eye hazards. For carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), endocrine disruption (EDC), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN), there is currently insufficient data (Tier 4) to make a confident assessment.
Q2: Magnesium hydroxide does not appear on major "Lists of Concern." However, this absence, coupled with the fact that many of its hazard categories are classified as data deficient, suggests that its overall risk profile may be understudied rather than confirmed safe across all potential hazard types.
Q3: Magnesium hydroxide is structurally well-characterized, possessing a precise molecular formula (H2MgO2) and classified as a "Small Molecule" rather than an incompletely defined substance. With 64,000 scientific references, it has been extensively studied in the literature. Nevertheless, despite this substantial research, the hazard profile for magnesium hydroxide remains incomplete, as five out of seven hazard categories are still categorized as data deficient.
